preregistration_status: Registered after source article and previously observed Kruger GPS displacement effect, BEFORE inspecting numeric original external-temperature values for this paired ecological analysis; deliberately exploratory and not an independent validation.
original_source: Source-verified Movebank DOI 10.5441/001/1.403h24q5, CC0, Kruger 14 female elephants each in a separate herd, GPS file bitstream 10240da1-0a99-42bf-a34f-eff15883bbfb, provider MD5 970ea06b9de69f1cc0d9f733d7f7e463, 43,776,326 bytes.
scientific_question: At equal daylength on opposite sides of Southern summer solstice, is the change in each elephant's difference between daytime and nighttime collar thermal conditions associated with its change in nighttime relative to daytime GPS displacement rate?
prior_artifact: The first source-verified Kruger hourly GPS result -0.028893655483298752 with 13 qualified animals was viewed. Reproduce its full value BEFORE reading numeric temperature values in the new route. Keep previous result unchanged.
sensor_interpretation: Source-paper Thaker et al 2019 DOI 10.3389/fevo.2019.00004 validated collar thermochron as indicator of RELATIVE ambient thermal variation; measured external-temperature mixes circuit-generated heat and the elephant's heat. It is not body temperature or absolute ambient air temperature. The paper already studied temperature-speed and water shuttling, so their simple relationship is NOT claimed as novel.
observation_alignment: Same hour-clock timestamp-only selection as Etosha elephant v1 and Kruger frozen v1; each 0.5–2 hour valid GPS interval has both endpoints/midpoint in same local solar daypart/date. Read collar temperature at the STARTING fix only, after positions determine the interval. Source temperatures not used in GPS interval inclusion, hour selection or date pairing.
source_temperature_qc: external-temperature units source-documented Celsius; accept finite -40 to 90 °C, retain missing/outside counts. Each daypart's temperature uses median of >=2 valid starting-fix temperature values among GPS-valid intervals; speeds use existing >=3 GPS intervals per daypart. Do not impute T.
astronomy: Use unchanged South December-solstice rising/falling pairing with <=5 minutes modeled photoperiod difference, >=30-day date gap, no date reuse, per part branch interval counts ratio within [0.5,2], >=10 GPS-qualified pairs per elephant-solar-year BEFORE requiring temperature.
thermal_predictor: x=falling-minus-rising [(median collar daytime T - median collar night T)], in °C. Positive x means daytime became thermally warmer RELATIVE to nighttime across the two matched solar days.
movement_response: y=falling-minus-rising [(log1p median GPS night step speed km/h) - (log1p median GPS day step speed km/h)] using the SAME preadmitted dates and samples.
independent_unit_and_model: For each elephant x southern solar-year with >=10 temperature-complete matched pairs and std dev(x)>=0.1°C, estimate within-year centered OLS slope cov(x,y)/var(x); average qualified year slopes equally within elephant; then average elephants equally within source. No p-value based on repeated GPS points/dates.
summaries: Report counts GPS-matched pairs, temperature-complete pairs, invalid/missing T observations, qualified individuals, individual slope +/- directions, source mean slope Δlog1p km/h per 1°C, 2000 animal-cluster-bootstrap percentile CI (seed 20261019). Also equal animal-weight mean ΔT_day, ΔT_night and relative thermal gradient, and equal animal-weight mean original paired y on sensor-covered days, separately labeled from the prior all-GPS estimate.
competing_explanations: Season, actual freshwater proximity, woody cover, breeding conditions, spatial moves and temperature-collar artefacts can jointly affect both signals; observational slopes are not causal thermoregulatory rates. Interpretation only conditional on Kruger source/2007–2009 study.
failure_policy: If fewer than 5 elephants with valid thermal variation, report INSUFFICIENT and all source support counts; never lower thresholds based on effects. Do not omit opposite or null individual slopes.
privacy: No individual IDs, precise positions, timestamps or source raw per-fix temperatures leave source runner. Reuse source citation and CC0 license statement.
